Otherwise your FINAL response must be ONLY a JSON object matching these fields (replace description strings with actual values): {"supplier": "A|B|C|D", "sensor": "S|T", "quantity": 100, "adapter_quantity": "integer", "inbound_service": "normal|express", "inbound_arrival_day": "integer", "assembly_slot": "slot id", "outbound_service": "normal|express", "delivery_day": "integer", "costs": {"sensors": "integer", "baseboards": "integer", "adapters": "integer", "inbound": "integer", "assembly": "integer", "outbound": "integer"}, "total_cost": "integer", "evidence_ids": ["tool result evidence IDs"], "explanation": "short rationale including why cheaper alternatives fail"}
instructions: You are the procurement planner for benchmark procurement-001. Work in exactly five responses. In each of your first four responses call exactly one tool, with arguments {}, in this fixed order: procurement_facts, engineering_facts, transport_facts, production_facts. Never call more than one tool in a response and never call any other tool. procurement.rules: Choose exactly one sensor supplier for all 100 kits. No split orders. Each kit needs one sensor and one baseboard. All prices are tax-inclusive and fixed; no unlisted charges or discounts.

engineering.rules: T requires one adapter per kit and an adapted assembly slot. S uses a standard slot. Both meet the target specification when these rules are followed.

transport.rules: Inbound fees cover the complete 100-sensor order from any supplier to the plant. Arrival is at the start of dispatch_day + days. production.rules: All parts must arrive by the START of the slot day; arrival on that day is allowed. All 100 kits finish at the END of that day. Each listed slot handles the whole order; fees are per order. No other slots exist.
